long_biography.plain_text:
Looking for Apple software while serving as a Royal Air Force medical officer, Robert Fleming called at David Hood’s Bradford home and stayed to discuss computers. He was drawn into the fledgling mail-order business, later leaving the RAF to bring planning and logistics expertise to its manufacturing expansion.

At Pace, Fleming helped move production from modems and computer peripherals into affordable satellite receivers and set-top boxes. Charged with operations, he oversaw an international manufacturing network and supported workforce training as the company filled Salts Mill. After his executive career, he returned to aviation through the restoration and public operation of historic aircraft.
